xingcheng-bpe-49k-mf2-v1.note: BPE exhausted mergeable pairs at freq>=2 - corpus ceiling for 64k is not reachable at mf=2

blueprint_item: X1 slice: 32k/64k vocab ratio (corpus governance remains gated on license ruling)

findings.allocation_shift: 32k: 3,028 cjk / 28,271 ascii tokens; 64k-mf1: 17,558 cjk / 44,828 ascii - new merges go mostly to zh multi-char tokens
findings.code_en_saturation: code-en bytes/token saturates ~4.2 at 32k (3.73->4.16->4.24->4.25); larger vocab adds almost nothing for code
findings.corpus_ceiling: first-party corpus saturates BPE merges at 49,270 (mf=2); reaching 64k requires mf=1 (freq-1 merges)
findings.implication_for_corpus_ruling: zh compression scales with vocab precisely because zh corpus is starved (21 docs); once licensed zh corpus lands (phase2r proposal pending), vocab should be retrained - current artifacts are interim

method.caveat_zh_sample: zh bucket is only ~12KB (21 zh-TW docs in corpus) - zh compression ratios are high-variance estimates
method.composition: per-token decode -> utf-8 byte class (cjk / ascii / other-utf8 / special)
method.compression: 400 random docs (seed=42) from corpus-v1 train.jsonl; doc language = zh iff CJK char share > 25%
method.corpus: xingcheng/runtime/corpus-v1 (star-corpus/v2, first-party-internal, 1769 docs, 15.2MB; language_stats code=1733 zh-TW=21 en=13)
method.training: native_transformer.bpe.train_bpe, byte-level BPE, same recipe family as existing artifacts

recommendation: keep xingcheng-bpe-64k-mf1-v1 as the 64k candidate (full vocab, best zh compression); 49k-mf2 retained as the mf=2 ceiling reference; retrain after corpus ruling lands
